key_insight: DanceOPD proposes a way to train one image generation model that can handle text-to-image creation, local editing, and global editing without these abilities constantly fighting each other. The core idea is to distill and align these capabilities on-policy so the model learns to compose them more consistently.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the conflict between different image generation capabilities: text-to-image generation often degrades when editing is added, and global editing can interfere with local editing. It targets the challenge of combining multiple generation/editing skills into a single model without performance loss.
method: Uses on-policy generative field distillation to align capabilities during training rather than treating them as separate tasks.
Trains the model to better balance text-to-image generation with both local and global editing behaviors.
Focuses on compositional capability learning so the model can preserve one skill while improving another.
impact: This matters for practitioners building unified image generation systems, since it offers a path to one model that can both generate and edit images reliably. It can simplify deployment and improve user experience by reducing the need for separate specialized models.
